title: SAGE-AIP: A Scale-Adaptive Gated Ensemble Framework for AI Adoption and Productivity Prediction-A Multi-Dataset Benchmark and Diagnostic Evaluation
content: This study audits three public datasets commonly framed as evidence about artificial   intelligence (AI) adoption and productivity and evaluates a reconstructed Scale-Adaptive Gated Ensemble Framework for AI Adoption and Productivity (SAGE-AIP) on the    employee-level dataset. The audit identifies three material measurement limitations: the 145,000-record adoption file has a distribution statistically indistinguishable from     Uniform(0,100) and negligible association with its recorded covariates; the country-year “AI productivity score” is an almost exact deterministic function of adoption, automation and output per worker; and recorded AI-tool information in the employee file is strongly associated with work location. Accordingly, the first two datasets are retained for    provenance and econometric diagnostics but are not used to support claims of predictive productivity gains. The employee benchmark uses 150 records, two repeats of shuffled three-fold outer cross-validation, two-fold inner tuning, identical data partitions across models, and employee-level paired bootstrap intervals based on 10,000 resamples. The corrected implementation uses nested cross-fitting: Ridge residual targets for each    gate-training fold are constructed using only that fold’s training observations. Random Forest achieved pooled RMSE 0.4935; the equal-weight residual ensemble achieved 0.4923; and full SAGE-AIP achieved 0.5024 (MAE 0.3759; R² 0.7683). The paired interval for the SAGE-AIP–Random Forest RMSE difference included zero, while full SAGE-AIP had slightly higher RMSE than the global-gate ablation. The group-stability penalty made a negligible difference. The findings do not establish predictive superiority for SAGE-AIP or a causal effect of AI use on productivity. The contribution is a transparent data-quality audit and a leakage-controlled evaluation of a reconstructed method, with limitations and unresolved provenance stated explicitly.
